NDT training in Idaho: how it works for Idaho employers and technicians

NDT training in Idaho is delivered by Atlantis NDT as ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET — live online for technicians anywhere in the state, from Boise to Coeur d’Alene to Pocatello, or onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you under its written practice after training, experience, exams and a vision test.

Idaho is a hard state to train in. Its industrial employers are spread across three regions separated by mountains and long drives. The Treasure Valley around Boise has semiconductor manufacturing, fabrication, food processing and aviation. North Idaho and the Panhandle have mining, forest products, hydro and pipelines. Southern and eastern Idaho have nuclear research, phosphate and fertiliser production, and large food-processing plants across the Magic Valley and upper Snake River plain. Few Idaho companies have enough technicians in one place to justify a full public course. Sending two people across the state, or out of state, to a classroom is expensive and takes them off the job.

So the Idaho model is simple. Theory is live online, wherever the technician is. Practical training and exams are onsite at the employer’s facility or at an arranged venue. Employers get technicians trained to their written practice and examined by a Level III. Individual technicians get training records and exam prep they can carry into a job. Atlantis has no training building in Idaho. Request an Idaho training quote. You will get cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Idaho

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A recommended structure for its method and level. It covers principles, equipment, calibration, technique, interpretation and codes, with supervised practical work.

MethodLevelsWhat Idaho employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, IIIThickness surveys on boilers, vessels and process piping in food, fertiliser and pulp plants; weld exams on new fabrication; penstock and hydro structure inspectionNone for Level I; Level II needs Level I plus documented experience per your written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, IICorrosion mapping on vessels and tanks, encoded weld inspection on pipelines and fabrication where codes allowNormally UT Level II first
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, IISizing flaws in heavy welds on vessels, penstocks and large structuresNormally UT Level II first
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, IIIWeld radiography on pipelines, process piping and pressure vessels during construction and repairNone for Level I training; NRC radiation safety rules apply separately
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, IIIStructural welds to AWS D1.1, mining equipment and hoists, crane and lifting gear, rail parts and heavy machineryNone for Level I
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, IIIStainless sanitary process piping in dairy and food plants, stainless welds, non-magnetic castings and aviation partsNone for Level I
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, IIIWeld visual inspection on fabrication, pipelines and structures; general condition assessment of plant equipmentNone for Level I
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, IIIHeat-exchanger tube inspection in process plants, surface crack checks on aircraft parts, conductivity sortingNone for Level I

Level III preparation for senior staff who will write procedures and certify technicians. See ASNT Level III training. Many small Idaho companies cannot justify a full-time Level III, which makes contracted Level III support (below) a practical option.

Which first? For plant maintenance roles in food, fertiliser and pulp, UT thickness and VT are most useful. For fabrication, MT and VT come first. For hydro and pipelines, UT and RT carry weight. Ask a Level III to suggest your sequence.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Idaho, step by step

  1. Employer written practice. This sets training, experience, exams, vision and recertification rules for each method and level.
  2. Formal classroom training. Delivered live online or onsite, with records per technician. For the recommended minimums, see the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Method and total NDT experience, logged under certified supervision. In Idaho this is often gained on plant maintenance inspections, shop QC or construction.
  4. General, specific and practical exams. All administered by a Level III. The practical exam uses real specimens representative of the work.
  5. Vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, recorded, usually every year.
  6. Employer certification. The certifying authority signs the record for each method and level.
  7. Recertification. Renewal on the interval set by the written practice.

Employers can find more in SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Idaho crews

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory for technicians anywhere in Idaho: Boise, Nampa, Meridian, Caldwell, Twin Falls, Burley, Pocatello, Idaho Falls, Lewiston, Moscow, Coeur d’Alene or Sandpoint. Idaho spans two time zones. The Panhandle is on Pacific time and most of the state on Mountain, and sessions are scheduled with that in mind. Documented attendance supports training records where your written practice allows online classroom delivery.
  • Onsite at your facility. Classroom and practical blocks at your plant, mine, shop or yard, on your equipment and specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight.
  • Blended. Online theory followed by a short onsite practical and exam block. This is often the best fit for Idaho employers with small, spread-out teams.

The practical exam is hands-on on real specimens. It cannot be done online. We schedule around harvest and processing seasons at food plants, planned outages at pulp and power plants, mine maintenance windows and the short construction season in the mountains. Ask about onsite training for your Idaho crew, or see live online NDT training and corporate programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Idaho

  • Treasure Valley. Semiconductor manufacturing and fab construction in Boise need weld and system inspection on high-purity process and utility piping. Fabrication shops, food processors and aviation also generate steady work. Mountain Home Air Force Base and the Idaho Air National Guard at Gowen Field bring military aviation maintenance to the region. That work usually follows military NDT requirements specified by the employer.
  • Hydroelectric power. Idaho relies heavily on hydro. Idaho Power’s Hells Canyon complex on the Snake River and federal dams such as Dworshak on the North Fork Clearwater have penstocks, gates, turbines and large welded structures. They need UT, MT, VT and sometimes RT during maintenance outages.
  • Food and dairy processing. The Magic Valley and the upper Snake River plain host large potato, dairy and food-processing plants. They run boilers, pressure vessels, ammonia refrigeration systems and stainless sanitary piping, which means UT thickness, PT and VT.
  • Phosphate and fertiliser. Southeast Idaho phosphate mining and processing, including the Pocatello area, involves corrosive process environments, tanks, vessels and heavy mobile equipment.
  • Mining and forest products. The Silver Valley in North Idaho has long-running underground mining with hoists, headframes and heavy equipment. Pulp, paper and wood-products mills in the north run boilers, digesters and pressure piping.
  • Nuclear research. Idaho National Laboratory near Idaho Falls is the state’s largest high-tech employer and has its own specialised NDT work. See our Idaho Falls NDT training page for the detail.
  • Pipelines and infrastructure. Interstate natural-gas transmission lines cross southern and northern Idaho. Pipeline construction and repair welds are inspected to API 1104. Highway and rail bridges are inspected to AWS D1.5 and the Idaho Transportation Department’s requirements.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Idaho’s Division of Building Safety runs the state boiler and pressure vessel safety programme. Its inspections are part of what drives periodic UT and VT at food and industrial plants. The state inspector is a separate role from the NDT technician, but they are often on site together.

Radiography licensing in Idaho. Idaho is not an NRC Agreement State. The NRC directly licenses radioactive material used for industrial radiography in Idaho, and 10 CFR Part 34 applies. Radiographers must be certified by an NRC-recognised certifying entity, such as ASNT’s Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel (IRRSP) programme. The state has jurisdiction over X-ray equipment. This is separate from your SNT-TC-1A RT method certification. Confirm current requirements with your employer’s radiation safety officer.

What Idaho employers typically ask for: method certification to their written practice, the ability to travel across the state or region, plant-specific safety orientations, and in mining, MSHA safety training. MSHA training is a federal mine safety requirement, not NDT training. Plan for these alongside your NDT hours.

Level III services and written practices for Idaho NDT companies

Many Idaho employers have a couple of NDT-certified staff but no full-time Level III. Their written practice may have been copied from a former employer or template years ago. The risk shows up when a customer, insurer or state inspector asks for the certification records and they do not hold up.

  • Written practice development: a written practice sized to a small or mid-sized Idaho company, covering only the methods and levels you perform.
  • Level III services on contract: procedure approval, exam administration and grading, certification record review, and periodic oversight. See SNT-TC-1A guidance.
  • Audit preparation before customer, insurer or registrar audits.
  • Onboarding for technicians hired from other employers, re-certified under your own written practice.

Book a Level III consultation for your Idaho programme.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical NDT, the Atlantis 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is useful for Idaho technicians who have limited hands-on time between remote jobs. The welding workshop and storage tank scenes are good rehearsal for fabrication and plant work. The simulator is practice only. It does not replace the practical exam on real specimens and does not count as experience. For theory, work through mock exams such as the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, examinations and Level III services for Idaho employers. See the full training catalogue.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Idaho

How do I get NDT certified in Idaho?

Complete formal training in your method and level, build documented experience under certified supervision, and pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III. Pass a vision exam, and your employer certifies you under its written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in Idaho?

Yes. Theory is delivered live online, so technicians anywhere in Idaho can attend, on either Pacific or Mountain time. The practical exam is hands-on, usually onsite at the employer’s facility under Level III oversight. See how online training works.

Is there an NDT school in Boise?

Atlantis has no campus in Boise or anywhere in Idaho. Training is live online and onsite at employers’ facilities. For employers, onsite delivery on their own equipment is usually more useful than a classroom anyway.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the training hours your written practice sets and on the documented experience you must build. See the training requirements matrix. The classroom is the short part.

Do I need a license for radiography in Idaho?

If you handle radioactive sources, yes. Idaho is not an Agreement State, so the NRC’s 10 CFR Part 34 applies, and radiographers need certification from an NRC-recognised body such as ASNT’s IRRSP. X-ray equipment falls under state jurisdiction. This is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification.

What does NDT training cost in Idaho?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size, delivery format and any Level III services. We return cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Request an Idaho training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Idaho employers?

SNT-TC-1A is widely used by US industrial employers, including in Idaho. Specific customers, the military, aerospace or nuclear programmes may add requirements. Check what your employer or contract specifies.

Which NDT method is most useful for Idaho jobs?

UT is the most versatile across hydro, plant maintenance, fabrication and pipelines. VT and MT are quick first certifications for fabrication and mining work. PT is valuable for stainless in food, dairy and semiconductor facilities.

Can you train our crew onsite in Twin Falls, Lewiston or Coeur d’Alene?

Yes. We deliver onsite across Idaho, on your equipment and specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight, scheduled around your operating season.

Can I get certified without an employer?

You can train and hold training records independently. SNT-TC-1A certification, though, is issued by an employer under its written practice.

Does Atlantis offer CWI, API or ISO 9712 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Those are separate schemes that some employers also ask for.

Is the simulator enough to pass the practical?

No. Practical NDT is for rehearsal only. Hands-on training and the practical exam must use real equipment and specimens.
